title: 39 Irresistible Bathtubs in Exquisitely Designed Spaces
summary: A sumptuous soak in the tub is an instant stress reliever and an escape from the everyday. Step inside these gorgeous bathrooms and start dreaming about a relaxing refuge of your own.
body_markdown:
Photo by Maxime Brouillet


In the primary suite of a largely[neutral-toned Toronto home](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/brunellos-home-ca/437052/) ,[EM Design Studio](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/elizabeth-metcalfe-interiors/) devised the kind of serene retreat that makes the distinction between bathing and living space seem arbitrary.


Warm French Vanilla marble and Moroccan Tadelakt plaster enfold the bath in a tranquil palette. A bespoke Atelier Février rug, a Fair Design[plaster side table](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/tables/side-tables/material/plaster/) , an[Apparatus](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/apparatus/) incense burner and[Waterworks](https://www.1stdibs.com/photos/creator/waterworks/) Henry fixtures add artisanal notes without disturbing the calm.


“Rather than introducing contrast through color or ornament, we looked to subtle shifts in texture, finish and form to give the room depth,” says Nicole Webster, the creative director and a partner at EM. The result is “quiet without feeling austere, luxurious without being overt and, above all, like a place you genuinely want to linger.”


---


Photo by Julie Soefer


[Marie Flanigan](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/marie-flanigan-interiors/) suffused a[Houston house with Provençal character](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/provence-inspired-estate-houston-tx/200762/) , layering natural materials and antique furnishings within its clean-lined light-filled architecture.


In the primary bathroom, the home’s general air of restraint makes way for one particularly striking vignette: a round[copper bathtub](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/copper-bathtub/) positioned beneath a[Paul Ferrante chandelier](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/paul-ferrante/furniture/lighting/chandeliers-pendant-lights/) and beside an[18th-century Italian giltwood mirror](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/18th-century-italian-wood-gilt-mirrors/) .


Burnished plaster walls along with reclaimed antique[marble flooring](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/marble-tile-flooring/) keep the composition grounded, while full-height[Kravet](https://www.1stdibs.com/dealers/kravet-inc/) drapery frames the arched window and its private-courtyard vista.


“A bathtub should feel like more than a functional fixture,” Flanigan says. “I want it to have a strong presence within the architecture while also creating a moment of respite — ideally positioned to take advantage of natural light or a meaningful view.”


---


Photo by Douglas Friedman


Designed by architect Harrie T. Lindeberg in the late 1920s, this[Seattle house](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/seattle-home-seattle-wa/330212/) occupies a dramatic perch overlooking Puget Sound. For its primary bathroom,[Clive Lonstein](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/clive-lonstein/) created a hexagonal space centered on a[freestanding tub](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/used-bathtubs/) .


Waterworks fixtures and white[Calacatta](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/calacatta-gold-marble/) Lincoln stone offer crisp counterpoints to the hand-polished[mahogany](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/material/mahogany/) walls, which, in turn, lend the room a vintage cruise-ship quality that nods to both the house’s Jazz Age origins and the homeowner’s career in the transportation industry.


“I loved the idea of being inspired by the ocean liners of the 1920s and 1930s,” Lonstein says. “You are transported when entering the bathroom into a gracious space that is traditionally inspired combined with modern elements.”


---


Throughout a[Gstaad vacation home](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/gstaad-ch/427292/) ,[Peter Mikic](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/peter-mikic-interiors/) paired rugged Alpine-chalet character with modern-day edginess and glamour. In this top-floor bathroom, a gleaming brass Catchpole & Rye tub makes a star turn against a pale-stone backdrop.


The pitched, timber-beamed ceiling keeps all that shine from feeling too glitzy, while a compact window lets in a wash of mountain light.


Even the practical details — like the[Art Deco](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/style/art-deco/) –inspired[THG Paris](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/building-garden/bathroom-fixtures/lalique-x-thg-paris-black-panther-bathroom-faucet-handles-france-2000s/id-f_51554332/) fittings, an unlaquered-brass towel warmer and a floating stone vanity — were deliberately considered. The space embodies what Mikic calls a “cozy masculine” aesthetic.


---


Photo by Rich Stapleton


Dean Levin and his[22RE](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/22re/) design team brought an updated[Mediterranean](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/mediterranean-furniture/) sensibility to a[1920s Los Angeles house](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/glendower-estate-los-angeles-ca/420292/) , using curved plaster and a consistent color and material palette throughout the interiors.


In the primary bath suite, sand-colored[tiles](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/floor-tiles/) line the tub and continue into the separate walk-in shower, imbuing it with a private-spa aura.


“We wanted the room feeling calm and connected to the natural light, which filters throughout the space,” Levin says. “The steps leading down to the drop-in tub add a more dramatic sense of arrival.”


---


Photo by Jorge Gera


This contemporary home on Florida’s Gold Coast “is a[modern take on a Moroccan riad](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/florida-modern-fort-lauderdale-fl/167882/) ,” says designer[Tom Stringer](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/tomstringer/) , who found glamorous ways to express that idea in the primary bathroom.


“Throughout the house and in the primary bath, rolling lattice panels that are modern takes on[traditional mashrabiya screens](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/mashrabiya-screen/) are used to divide the room and to filter the strong sunlight,” Stringer explains.


A Bain Ultra soaking tub rests atop a perimeter drain filled with polished stones, all surrounded by[white coral](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/white-coral/) flooring, the combination giving the room an elemental character.[Wenge cabinetry](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/storage-case-pieces/cabinets/material/wenge/) and a lightly aged[brass pendant](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/lighting/chandeliers-pendant-lights/material/brass/) add warmth.


A[Holly Hunt](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/holly-hunt/furniture/) bench and three-tier[Dessin Fournir](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/dessin-fournir/furniture/) side table, meanwhile, demonstrate that even a plumbed nest can display the comfortable sophistication of a high-end living room.


Finally, *Beautiful Monster* , a[surreal photograph](https://www.1stdibs.com/art/photography/style/surrealist/) by Paco Peregrín, “anchors the space,” says Stringer. The effect is worldly without feeling too thematic.


---


Photo by Luis Ridao


“Historic” barely skims the surface in describing a home in London’s Bloomsbury, to which 1stDibs 50 honoree Rachel Chudley brought her special touch.


“Virginia Woolf danced in the kitchen of this house!” says Chudley. “It is a wonderful place with a special creative heritage — and creative current inhabitants. My goal was to reflect this in the design decisions we made.”


One ravishing result of these design decisions is seen here: a combination **[dressing room, bath and entertaining space](https://www.1stdibs.com/1stdibs-50/design-firm/rachel-chudley-2021/) sporting an Eloise Fornieles painting above the fireplace.


---


Photo by Björn Wallander


In the main bathroom on the third floor of a five-story townhouse in[downtown Manhattan](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/west-eleventh-street-residence-new-york-ny/207152/) , architect Rafael de Cárdenas employed a palette of grays, which, he explains, “mediates between the cooler shades of the floors above and the warmer ones on the floors below.”


A black-and-white[Horst P. Horst](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/horst-p-horst/) photograph behind the tub adds contrast to the monochromatic theme.


---


Photo by Tria Giovan


In designing this space in a[Smith Lake, Alabama,](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/smith-lake-project/68903/)[vacation home](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/smith-lake-project/68903/) , Andrew Brown took his cue from the surrounding nature. “I wanted the colors of the bathroom to complement, but not distract from, the outdoors,” he says. “The view is really the main feature in the bathroom, and the tub provides the perfect space to relax and enjoy the views.”


To keep the focus on the lake-scape, Brown settled on a subtle decor, including an antique English[bamboo side table](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/tables/material/bamboo/) topped by a vintage[glass vase](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/decorative-objects/vases-vessels/material/glass/) .


---


Photo by Pieter Estersohn


“The client wanted a tub to share, so I built a room around this marble custom surround,” Mona Hajj says, describing the super-chic bath she designed for an[early-20th-century house in Baltimore](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/baltimore-md--baltimore-md/143621/) .


And the qualities that characterize her creation? “Luxury and comfort that came about by combining modern and old features — a good marriage,” says Hajj, who satisfied the “old” side of that equation with graceful antiques like the English pier mirror.


---


Photo by Pieter Estersohn


For clients who wanted the bath in their[Malibu](https://www.1stdibs.com/photo/beach-style-bathroom-malibu-ca/4197681/) beach house to serve as a calm retreat, Giannetti Home created a space with a soothing, neutral palette and a decor of understated elegance.


“The large arched window connects the space to the beautiful landscape,” says Brooke Giannetti. “And the antique Swedish[baroque stool](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/seating/stools/style/baroque/) is a wonderful juxtaposition against the more-clean-lined elements in the room.”


---


Photo by Julie Soefer


“The inspiration for this[Houston bathroom](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/transitional-paradise--houston-tx/208882/) was the gorgeous marble we found,” says Chandos Dodson. Dodson deployed the luxe material to craft a light, bright, yet warm space, furnished with such similarly sumptuous elements as a Janet Wiebe[Murano glass chandelier](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/lighting/chandeliers-pendant-lights/material/murano-glass/) and an ottoman locally made by Joseph Company.


---


Photo by Phillip Durrant


[Studio Ashby](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/studio-ashby/projects/) created a spa-like bathroom in a London apartment perched 41 stories above the Thames. Designer Sophie Ashby’s favorite element? Tim Hall’s seascape photograph, strategically placed to serve as a transportive focal point for someone serenely soaking in the tub.


---


Marco Ricca


“The Arabescato marble reminds me of old European bathrooms,” says Michelle Gerson, explaining how the material set the scene for this zen space in[her own New Jersey home](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/michelle-gerson-home-new-york-ny/209792/) . “We toned the wild stone down with modern lacquer cabinetry, large organic concrete tiles and a modern bathtub.”


A touch of romance is added by the large-scale artwork, a multicolored love poem by Matthew Heller.


---


Photo by N. Johnson, B. Ambridge, J. Thornton


“I love it when clients are open to doing something that hasn’t been done before. Here, the goal was to create something dramatic and irreverent,” Summer Thornton says of this bathroom in a[Lincoln Park, Chicago, home](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/lincoln-park-vintage-chicago-il/44263/) , which features Cowtan & Tout wallpaper and a custom-painted floor. “Is it over the top? Yes! And that’s the point. But it is done in a whimsical way with tongue firmly planted in cheek.


“When you walk in, you can’t help but be energized and transported to a fantasy world — perfect for a lazy Sunday afternoon of daydreaming in the tub.”


---


Photo by Grey Crawford


“The client wanted a beautiful feminine bathroom with a slightly European flair,” says Jeff Andrews, who designed this space in a[Los Angeles](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/los-angeles--hidden-hills-ca/683/) home. “We ultimately went with classic finishes and furnishings for a serene and timeless look.” The chaise, which is upholstered in[Schumacher fabric](https://www.1stdibs.com/introspective-magazine/dara-caponigro/) , is from[Eloquence](https://www.1stdibs.com/dealers/eloquence/) ; the wallpaper is Cowtan & Tout.


---


Photo by Roger Davies


A[glass star pendant](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/lighting/chandeliers-pendant-lights/tunisian-deep-blue-glass-pendant-star-shape-handmade-ceiling-lamp-light/id-f_7465983/) hangs over the tub in a the bathroom of[Martyn Lawrence Bullard–designed 1929 villa in Los Angeles](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/villa-luna-west-hollywood-ca/7153/) . The cabinets are fronted in[Missoni](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/missoni/furniture/) fabric.


---


Photo by Debbie Patterson


“The clients wanted a ‘romantic bathroom’ in this space,” Robert Young, of Riviere Interiors, says of this[1670 London townhouse](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/-charles-ii-period-townhouse-london-gb/2333/) .


“We installed a good sized en suite bathroom off the other side of their master bedroom, and this one was created in a small space that used to be a closet. We installed a vintage mid-century candlelight chandelier and a pair of fine early 19th-century cut-glass wall lights in this space, beside and in front of a French silvered cushion moulded mirror, circa 1890. The walls and floor are clad in polished black marble.”


---


Photo by Nick Johnson


“My client wanted his home to feel like a country retreat in the city,” James Huniford says of this[Manhattan penthouse](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/bond-street-new-york-ny/43903/) , “so we incorporated pipe-like fittings by Rocky Mountain Hardware and installed a carved cedar tub by E-Legno. A series of healthy-living affirmations hangs on the wall above.”


---


Photo by Simon Upton


Hubert Zandberg designed this[Georgian townhouse](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/regents-park-grand-house-london-gb/4333/) in London with a 1940s French aesthetic, and the marble master bath features glamorous elements like crystal chandelier and sconces and a mirror-paneled tub.


---


Photo by Rikki Snyder


Timothy Godbold designed this[Sag Harbor, New York](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/262-north-haven-sag-harbor-ny/29273/) , home with industrial influences, including the bronze fittings and accessories in the bathroom. The sconces, wooden vanity and large baskets also lend the space a vintage,[farmhouse](https://www.1stdibs.com/blogs/the-study/farmhouse-style/) feel.


---


Photo by Ryan Phillips


“This is a master bathroom exclusively for the lady of the house,” Deirdre Doherty says of this Spanish Colonial home in the[Los Feliz](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/los-feliz-spanish-los-angeles-ca/9153/) area of Los Angeles. “The style is a loose take on French 1940s with an unashamed burst of glamour befitting Wallis Simpson in Paris to Rita Hayworth in Hollywood.”


The room includes a vintage[Baccarat](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/baccarat/furniture/) chandelier, contemporary Baccarat wall lights and[René Lalique](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/rene-lalique/furniture/)


accessories.


---


Photo by Mark Jenkinson


“The overall intention was to include the landscape as one of the dominant design elements to create a wholly indoor-outdoor bathroom,” says Taryn Christoff of Christoff:Finio Architecture, who designed this home on Long Island’s[East End](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/east-end-house-long-island/5093/) .


“To further that ambition, the cast bronze panels extend from inside of the bathroom to the exterior — to become weathered naturally by the ocean air. The soaking tub is a simple and restful white shape in contrast to the colors and textures of the site.” The chairs on the patio outside the bathroom are by Janus et Cie.


---


Photo by Lisa Romerein


At[Patina Farm](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/patina-farm-ojai-ca/8393/) in Ojai, California, the residence of design duo Brooke and Steve Giannetti, the tub is located in the glass-walled shower room, which offers views of the garden.


---


Photo by Francis Amiand


[Bismut & Bismut](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/apartment-001-paris-fr/4123/) aimed to contrast the very traditional bathroom design with[contemporary](https://www.1stdibs.com/blogs/the-study/contemporary-vs-modern/) elements, including furniture and the ceiling, for this Paris apartment. A vintage chandelier purchase at a flea market hangs over the space, which features an arm chair by[Charles Eames](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/charles-eames/furniture/) and[Eero Saarinen](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/eero-saarinen/furniture/)


.


---


Photo by Scott Frances


A[Fontana Arte chandelier](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/fontana-arte/) in oxidized bronze clear and frosted glass hangs in the sleek master bath of this[Upper East Side penthouse](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/upper-east-side-penthouse-new-york-ny/8443/) by Thad Hayes. The designer also created the custom cabinet.


---


Photo by Jonathan Wallen


At this[shingle-style](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/shingle-style-house-lincolnville-us/4773/) summer home in Maine, designed by Peter Pennoyer Architects and decorated by[Jayne Design Studio](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/penobscot-bay-house-liberty-me/7463/) , the window above the tub offers sweeping ocean views. The wallpapered ceiling and embroidered rug add vintage appeal to the new-construction house.


---


Photo by Anastassio Mentis


Groves & Co. created a sophisticated bathroom suite in this[New York duplex](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/park-avenue-residence-new-york-ny/6342/) , including walnut paneling and heavily grained travertine countertops. The[hand-carved wooden stool](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/seating/stools/carol-egan-sculptural-hand-carved-walnut-stool-united-states-2012/id-f_719635/) is by Carol Egan and was sourced at[Maison Gerard](https://www.1stdibs.com/dealers/maison-gerard/) .


---


Photo by Michael Moran


“The bathroom, located in one of[Park Avenue](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/park-avenue-duplex-new-york-us/2863/) ’s most prestigious and exclusive buildings, was designed for a young mother,” according to Fox-Nahem Associates, who designed the space. “The marble wall panels set into a satin nickel frame is a nod to the pre-war heritage of the building, but executed in a cleaner way to reflect the aesthetic of the client.


Using traditional materials in a modern way keeps the final result fresh and contemporary.” A 1960s glass and chrome Fontana Arte chandelier hangs over the space.


---


Photo by Richard Powers


Kelly Behun designed this[Manhattan penthouse](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/park-ave-penthouse-new-york-ny/44163/) , which is located at the top of Rafael Viñoly’s 432 Park Avenue, the tallest residential building in the Western Hemisphere. The bathroom’s clean lines and neutral palette keeps the attention on the expansive city views.


---


Photo by Laure Joliet


“Since the local landscape is truly one of a kind, we used that as a touchstone for the design scheme, building a seamless transition between indoors and out,” Nicole Hollis says of this space at[Carmel Valley Ranch](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/carmel-valley-ranch-carmel-valley-ca/2143/) in California, which has a custom bathtub by the designer.


“This concrete soaking tub is located on the patio and extends the use of the space and encourages the residential feel. All the natural textures and tones connect directly with the landscape and the view.”


---


Photo by Eric Laignel


Boldly patterned encaustic tiles pop in this elegant[West Village townhouse](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/west-village-town-house-new-york-ny/50853/) ‘s bathroom by Mark Zeff, which features a neutral palette with silver accents.


---


Photo by Matt Weir


Brown Design Group’s Ryan Brown and Diego Monchamp were inspired by their love of the Hamptons when decorating this home in[Dana Point, California](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/beachview-dana-point-ca/3483/) . The bathroom, whose tub is positioned in front of a wide ocean-facing window, features a sitting area in front of the dramatic fireplace.


---


Photo by Evan Joseph


“A porcelain Cheviot tub is set in concrete to reveal its sinuous curves and reference the raw concrete loft space on the floor below of the duplex penthouse,” Michael Haverland says of this New York[duplex loft](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/duplex-loft-new-york-ny/54323/) he designed. “ The bluestone floor weaves through a steel and glass wall to engage the large terrace and soothing green tile references nature.”


---


Photo by William Waldron


Ike Kligerman Barkley designed this[New England beach house](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/overlook-house-new-england-ma/6673/) , whose restrained interiors feature clean lines and light finishes. A photograph by Olaf Otto Becker hangs above the fireplace.


---


Photo by Brantley Photography


“Set in the master suite of a vacation home in[Naples, Florida](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/naples-florida-vacation-home-fort-myers-fl/44143/) , this bathroom’s mood is serene and relaxing,” Summer Thornton says of the space decorated with an iron lantern by Circa Lighting and a garden stool. “It’s t he perfect place for a bubble bath and a glass of wine after a day of fun in the sun.”


---


Photo by Mark Adams


“The bathroom has a lot of glass and marble, so the look is minimal, but not cold,” Nicole Hollis says of a renovated, architecturally significant[San Francisco](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/telegraph-hill-residence-san-francisco-ca/8843/) residence by Jim Jennings. “ The veining of the Calcutta marble adds warmth. And there is a lot of wood. We kept the original maple floors and did custom walnut cabinetry.


The windows were sandblasted for privacy, but no other window treatments are used. So natural light is used to its full advantage. These elements all work together to create a space that is bright, relaxing and welcoming throughout the day.”


---


Photo by Max Kim-Bee


“The interiors of this Northern California home reflect the subtle beauty of its natural surroundings with a nod to the California’s[Arts & Crafts](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/style/arts-and-crafts/) movement,” James Huniford says of this home in California’s[Marin County](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/marin-county-san-rafael-us/1573/) . “ The couple wanted a structure that would feel ‘tucked in’ by the site’s 125-foot redwoods and oak trees.”
